newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger raises Southam stake to 58.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger raises Southam stake to 58.6 pct.

text.p: Hollinger Inc said on Thursday it purchased 6,552,445 common shares of Southam Inc under its recent failed takeover offer, bringing its ownership stake in Southam to 45,692,488 common shares, or about 58.6 percent.
The international publisher, controlled by press baron Conrad Black, said in a statement it "has no current plans to acquire additional Southam common shares."

Hollinger's C$23.50 cash-and-stock bid to take Southam private, which expired July 7, failed after only about six million or 15.6 percent of minority Southam shares were tendered to the offer. A condition of the bid required at least 66.67 percent of minority shares to be tendered for the bid to succeed.
Prior to the recent takeover offer, Hollinger owned about 50.45 percent of the newspaper chain.

Toronto-based Southam is Canada's largest newspaper chain by circulation, publishing 58 free and paid circulation newspapers and 32 dailies, including the Montreal Gazette, the Ottawa Citizen and Vancouver Sun.
Hollinger's holdings include several high-profile international papers including London's Daily Telegraph, the Chicago Sun-Times and Jerusalem Post.
